evidence: Route 1 (per-item published statistics), decisive form. The preprint's Table 6 publishes a full GRM solution per item -- one discrimination plus FIVE beta thresholds, 36 numbers. Refitting a unidimensional graded response model (mirt, EM) on the live IRW data reproduces every one: alpha pub/live 1.47/1.47, 2.10/2.10, 1.69/1.69, 2.45/2.45, 2.48/2.48, 2.09/2.09; e.g. sabas3 betas pub -0.04/0.68/1.22/2.00/2.67 vs live -0.04/0.68/1.22/2.00/2.67. Largest absolute deviation across all 36 parameters = 0.0047. The match is item-specific, not a global fit: each live item's 6-number signature is nearest its OWN published row, self-distance 0.006-0.009 against next-best 0.296-0.769, so every item is distinguished from every other and no pair is confusable. The row-number -> wording step is explicit in the source rather than inferred: Table 6 labels its rows 'Most important thing', 'Conflicts have arisen', 'Preoccupying myself', 'Fiddle around more', 'Irritable', 'Fail to use less', each a fragment of exactly one item of Csibi et al. (2018) Appendix 1, in that order. Corroboration: live per-item means 2.00/1.63/2.15/1.82/1.78/1.90 average to 1.88 against the preprint's Table 2 SABAS mean 1.88 (SD 1.33), and Cronbach alpha 0.81 against the published 0.81. Second axis (option_text<->resp) is published, not inferred: Csibi et al. (2018) Appendix 1 prints the numerals 1..6 under the six anchors Strongly Disagree..Strongly Agree, and the preprint states higher scores = greater addiction risk; all 36 GRM thresholds increase monotonically with resp, consistent. NOT established: the administered Chinese wording (published nowhere in the deposit or the preprint, so the canonical English ships as a translated_substitute), and hence whether the Chinese translation the children read diverges in wording from the English shipped here. Two prose sentences in the preprint's Results contradict its own Table 6 (the discriminations listed 'highest to lowest' are in ascending order, and item 2 is said to have the highest difficulty for 'strongly agree' where Table 6 gives that to item 1), so they were deliberately NOT used as tests; the 36 tabulated numbers were.

evidence: Deposit labels: both .sav files label all 6 PDTS columns with an English item text prefixed by the column's own code (12/12 prefix matches), tying PDTS2 to 'no control over ICT implemented changes' and PDTS3 to 'irritated in connection to new ICT solutions'. The paper disagrees for exactly these two: Table 2/Table 4/body number 'irritated' item 2 and 'no control' item 3, and Table 2's M/SD are the column-order means of the Study 1 file (2.90/2.93/2.84/2.90/2.35/2.34 printed vs 2.8909/2.9273/2.8402/2.8813/2.3500/2.3394 computed), so one of the two sources has rows 2 and 3 crossed. Discriminating check (route 8/1): the undisputed 'upset' item PDTS1 correlates more with PDTS3 than with PDTS2 in both independent samples - Study 1 r=0.783 vs 0.733 (diff +0.050), Study 2 r=0.660 vs 0.611 (diff +0.049) - as expected if PDTS3 is the near-synonym 'irritated' item, i.e. the .sav labelling. Live IRW per-item means reproduce the s003 column means to 0.00e+00 for all 6 items (2.433692, 2.516129, 2.500000, 2.442652, 2.241935, 2.234767), so the melt preserved the column-to-code tie. What this does NOT establish: a ~0.05 correlation margin does not conclusively separate PDTS2 from PDTS3, so those two codes are not distinguished outright; PDTS1, PDTS4, PDTS5 and PDTS6 are pinned by content and agreed by both sources. Hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED.
